item.title: Hotel workers' skills put to the test at 36th Annual Housekeeping Olympics in Las Vegas
item.description: Hotel workers from across the country gathered in Las Vegas for the 36th annual Housekeeping Olympics, turning everyday duties into a series of fast-paced competitions.
item.content:encoded:
Hotel workers put their housekeeping skills to the test earlier this week in Las Vegas at the 36th annual International Sanitary Supply Association (ISSA) Housekeeping Olympics.

Ten teams competed Monday at Michelob ULTRA Arena at Mandalay Bay Resort and Casino in eight events that turned routine cleaning duties into fast-paced challenges testing speed, precision and teamwork.

The competition is organized by the ISSA, which is a global trade association for the cleaning industry. 

Michael Patterson, executive director of the Indoor Environmental Healthcare & Hospitality Association, a division of ISSA, said the competition began 36 years ago to recognize housekeeping employees and give them an event of their own.

F1 LEGEND RICCARDO PATRESE TALKS ABOUT F1'S FIRST FAILED ATTEMPT AT RACING IN LAS VEGAS: ‘IT WAS A CAR PARK’

"The housekeepers are always the unsung heroes, whether they're in hospitality or whether they're in health care," Patterson said.

The contests included a two-minute bed-making challenge, a mop relay, a vacuum cleaner race and a pad toss. A new triathlon-style event combined glass cleaning, a stain section and a paper towel toss.

Some of the loudest cheers came during the spirit dance competition. Judges watched as teams danced choreographed performances complete with dazzling costumes and complete sets. Many teams leaned into the themes of their hotels and the glamour of the Las Vegas Strip.

Team Luxor took the floor first in mummy costumes inspired by the ancient Egyptian theme of the Luxor Hotel and Casino.

The team's choreographer told Fox News she wanted to keep the routine accessible to everyone.

"We wanted moves that everybody can do," she said.

When the final scores were tallied, a team of South Dakota hotel workers competing for the first time took home the championship.

US WARNS AMERICANS IN KEY LOCATIONS TO ‘KEEP A LOW PROFILE’ AHAD OF CROWDED HOLIDAY TRAVEL

LIV Hospitality finished first overall, followed by Excalibur Hotel in second place and Mandalay Bay in third, according to the company's announcement. The South Dakota team also won the mop relay and toilet paper toss.

The victory capped LIV Hospitality's statewide Road to Vegas Housekeeping Championship Series. The company held regional competitions before hosting a final at The Box Elder Events Center. Top competitors earned spots on the team that traveled to Las Vegas.

Rather than representing one hotel, the team brought together employees from multiple properties across South Dakota. They competed against workers from Las Vegas resorts including Bellagio, The Cosmopolitan, Luxor and MGM Grand.

"We went to Las Vegas proud to represent South Dakota. Coming home as the overall champions makes this incredibly special," Kayti Ratigan, LIV Hospitality's chief of operations, said in the company's announcement.

"Our team competed against some of the best hospitality professionals in the industry, and they showed exactly what we already knew: There is tremendous talent, pride and professionalism right here in South Dakota," Ratigan said.

For LIV Hospitality team member Adrianna Young Bear, making it to Las Vegas was an achievement in itself. She said she had followed the competition for years before her team finally got the opportunity to participate.

"I've been following the housekeeping competition for years. We finally made it here," Young Bear said. "This was a long journey for us to get here, and we finally did."

Young Bear said seasonal tourism can make it difficult to recruit and retain hospitality workers in South Dakota. She said the competition gave the group an opportunity to recognize the contributions of those employees.

"We are the backbone to every local town across the United States, across the world," Young Bear said.

SKYDIVING INJURY LEAVES 24-YEAR-OLD TOURIST STRANDED IN AUSTRALIA ON MEDICAL NO-FLY LIST

Over the years, the competition has also attracted attention beyond the hospitality industry. ISSA estimated that the 2025 event generated more than 50 million views and 750,000 social media engagements.

In August 2026, the competition made its ESPN8: The Ocho debut at ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex at Walt Disney World Resort as part of the network's celebration of unconventional sports and competitions.

A member of the Bellagio team said the event gave employees a chance to celebrate their work with colleagues from other hotels. The team practiced weekly for months, increasing rehearsals in the final weeks before the competition.

"It's an amazing experience for everybody to be able to see the hard work all the team members do on a daily basis," the team member said. "It's just for fun here, but they do this every day."

item.title: Trump's massive DC triumphal arch project dealt another blow by federal judge
item.description: A federal judge extended her order blocking construction of President Donald Trump's triumphal arch in Washington, D.C., putting the project on hold until at least Dec. 3.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington in Washington, D.C., was dealt another blow Wednesday when a federal judge extended an order blocking construction until at least early December.

U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended her initial Nov. 5 temporary restraining order blocking construction of the arch for another 14 days, delaying progress on the structure until at least Dec. 3.

The extension comes as Chutkan's original order was set to expire Thursday.

The judge said the extension would give her additional time to consider lawsuits filed by the District of Columbia and Virginia seeking a longer-term injunction against the project.

MULTIPLE KENNEDY FAMILY MEMBERS SEEK TO JOIN LEGAL BATTLE AGAINST TRUMP'S TRIUMPHAL ARCH

The order marks the latest setback for one of the president's major projects in the nation's capital. Inspired by Paris' Arc de Triomphe, the proposed monument would stand near the Memorial Bridge, which connects Arlington National Cemetery to Washington, D.C.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, the White House criticized the order, saying the project was being undercut by an "activist district court."

"The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation," White House spokesman Davis Ingle said.

"We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds," he added.

EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE

Chutkan issued the temporary restraining order earlier this month just hours after the National Capital Planning Commission approved the project.

The approval had cleared the way for construction to begin before the court intervened.

Trump has previously said the triumphal arch would be converted into a military complex capable of rapidly deploying large numbers of drones, with snipers positioned on the roof and plaza areas.

He also said the complex would store "large quantities of sniper ammunition."

The project has drawn criticism from preservationists, lawmakers and veterans, who argue that it could disrupt views of the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

Last week, nine members of the Kennedy family also sought to stop the project, saying it would obstruct views and cast shadows over their relatives' grave sites at Arlington National Cemetery.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: 'You will regret it': Angry resident confronts Democratic mayor during chaotic council meeting
item.description: Video captured a California immigration activist threatening to reveal Mayor Kevin McCarty's home address at a Sacramento City Council meeting after becoming angry with city policies.
item.content:encoded:
A Sacramento City Council meeting descended into chaos Tuesday after an angry resident threatened the Democratic mayor's political career and attempted to publicly reveal his home address, prompting officials to cut her microphone and temporarily recess the meeting.

Video from Tuesday's city council livestream reviewed by Fox News Digital showed a woman confronting Sacramento Mayor Kevin McCarty during the public comment portion of the meeting, warning that protesters would continue disrupting city business if officials failed to address their concerns.

"If you do not vote in our interest again, you will regret it," the woman said. "We protest. We stop things. We shut things down, Kevin. And careers."

The woman then suggested that McCarty's political career had run its course.

MEMPHIS CITY COUNCIL DEVOLVES INTO CHAOS AFTER DATA CENTER MORATORIUM VOTE POSTPONED

"It's time for your f---ing career to end," she said, before raising the possibility of his retirement.

As council officials repeatedly attempted to restore order, someone in the audience also urged the angry woman to show decorum.

"F--- your decorum," she responded.

The confrontation escalated further when the woman threatened to disclose the mayor's home address.

"I do not give a f--- about your privacy," she shouted. "Do you want everyone to know your address? Because now I know your address."

Her microphone appeared to be cut as she began reciting what she claimed was the mayor's address, and a council official warned her against disclosing private information.

'I BASICALLY SNAPPED': NEW JERSEY MAYOR CHARGES AT RESIDENT DURING CHAOTIC COUNCIL MEETING

As shouting erupted in the council chambers, officials called a recess and council members left the dais.

Approximately 20 minutes later, council members returned and resumed public comment. No audience members were removed, The Sacramento Bee reported.

According to the newspaper, the confrontation with the woman, identified by the outlet as a local immigration activist, unfolded amid ongoing tensions over the city's immigration enforcement policies and its cooperation with federal authorities.

Earlier in the meeting, McCarty announced that the council would postpone consideration of a $3.7 million Department of Homeland Security grant agreement amid questions about potential data-sharing provisions.

Tuesday's incident marked the fifth time this year that Sacramento City Council members had recessed a meeting because of audience disruptions, according to The Sacramento Bee. The repeated confrontations have largely stemmed from activists' concerns about immigration enforcement and the city's sanctuary policies, the outlet reported.

DEMOCRAT MAYOR BLASTED BY DHS FOR 'HUNTING DOWN' PROPERTY OWNERS LEASING TO ICE: 'UNHINGED'

The mayor's office declined to comment on the incident to Fox News Digital.

This week's outburst comes months after Fox News Digital reported that a live microphone captured McCarty and Vice Mayor Karina Talamantes discussing whether disruptive protesters could be barred from future council meetings.

"We should go over this disruptions thing, because if we want to ban somebody in the future, like to take them out, we have to point out specifically," Talamantes was heard saying during the July meeting.

"I know, but the city attorney said we can't do that," McCarty responded.

The woman who confronted McCarty on Tuesday also appeared during the July meeting, when she shouted at the mayor, "Kevin, listen to me. Stop being an a--hole, dude. Listen to your f---ing constituents."

Following the July incident, McCarty told Fox News Digital that council leaders were responsible for ensuring public meetings remained accessible and orderly.

Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price contributed to this report.

item.title: WNBA launches search for next commissioner, but outgoing Cathy Engelbert could stay into 2027
item.description: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert says more than a dozen candidates are in the mix to succeed her, with officiating and player relations among top issues.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA's search for Cathy Engelbert’s successor has officially kicked off. According to reports, the league will work to eventually narrow down a list of more than a dozen candidates.

Engelbert’s eight-year, at-times tumultuous tenure is nearing its end, but she could remain in the role beyond 2026 if the search extends into 2027.

Engelbert previously announced plans to retire at the end of the year but clarified that she would remain commissioner beyond Dec. 31 if a successor was not in place. She took over as commissioner in 2019.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Monday marked Engelbert’s final WNBA Board of Governors meeting. Representatives from all 15 current teams attended, along with officials from the three expansion franchises set to join the league over the next four years: Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver also attended.

That meeting came a few days after Engelbert met with coaches, general managers and team presidents last week at the WNBA offices for the annual competition committee meetings.

If the WNBA chooses not to extend Engelbert’s tenure beyond Dec. 31, it could consider NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum. Tatum served as interim WNBA commissioner for nine months before Engelbert was hired following Lisa Borders’ departure in 2018.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SAYS SHE'S TALKED WITH NBA COMMISSIONER ADAM SILVER AMID SEARCH FOR WNBA'S NEXT COMMISSIONER

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The next commissioner of the league will inherit a host of issues, including officiating, the transgender debate, scheduling and improving a strained relationship with players.

The league thrived in many ways during Engelbert’s tenure. Under her leadership, the WNBA enjoyed record growth and popularity, and signed a record-breaking broadcasting deal. Players surpassed $1 million in annual salaries.

WNBA EXPANDS REGULAR SEASON TO 50 GAMES STARTING IN 2027, THE LONGEST SCHEDULE IN LEAGUE HISTORY

But despite her accomplishments, Engelbert’s relationship with players was cordial at best, confrontational at other times. New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart may have summed it up best when said players "respect" Engelbert.

Late last month, Engelbert presented the WNBA championship trophy to the Golden State Valkyries after they defeated the Atlanta Dream in the league’s first Finals series to reach seven games.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Lane Kiffin’s roster fight set the stage, Will Wade just threw a grenade in LSU-SEC war with RJ Luis
item.description: Will Wade sent RJ Luis onto the court against Louisiana-Monroe, escalating LSU's legal war with the SEC after a judge granted the former pro an injunction.
item.content:encoded:
The LSU Tigers officially escalated the legal battle with the SEC on Wednesday night when basketball coach Will Wade sent RJ Luis Jr. off the bench and into the game against Louisiana-Monroe.

Over the past five days, 19th Judicial District Court Judge William Jorden of Baton Rouge granted RJ Luis a preliminary injunction that allowed the LSU Tigers to roster the former professional athlete.

This whole saga stems from the former St. John's player returning to college for another season, after already declaring for the draft following his final game at the collegiate level in March 2025. After signing a 2-way deal at the NBA level, Luis was seeking a return to college, and signed with LSU last spring.

Luis went undrafted in 2025, then ended up signing a 2-way contract with the Utah Jazz.

LSU LATEST BASKETBALL PROGRAM TO TAP INTO G LEAGUE RANKS, SIGNING FORMER PRO GUARD RJ LUIS JR

But, there have always been rules about former professional athletes coming back to college, though that did not stop Will Wade from recruiting RJ Luis to play basketball at LSU after the head coach returned to Baton Rouge.

And, for all of those that thought this was about college football, you were sorely mistaken.

"I'm gonna refer to our university statement from yesterday. I'll be happy to answer any questions on how he played. "Everybody we played tonight is eligible," Will Wade said postgame. 

Over the past three months, LSU had already been fighting the SEC and NCAA over its rules about athletes pursuing an additional year of eligibility based upon the new guidelines that were enacted around players having five years to play five seasons of competition.

This has led to the LSU athletic department having to make a decision on whether to roster two football players one day before the Tigers faced Clemson in Baton Rouge.

Ultimately, the Tigers' administration decided against officially adding the players to the roster.

LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN

That did not stop the legal saga around both LSU and the SEC, after the conference was enjoined in a lawsuit filed by the football players in September that then led to commissioner Greg Sankey taking the stand inside a Baton Rouge courtroom.

Fast-forward two months, and the same situation has been playing out around the basketball court pertaining to RJ Luis.

"They [LSU] are hiding behind a judge, and I don't know why they think they won't ultimately find a way to punish them," one Power-four head basketball coach told OutKick. "They are actually going to fight the conference over one player and watch the world burn in the process?

"I guess they are really not worried about the fallout, because this makes the whole administration look petty. No matter how you feel about the SEC, it's obvious how they [LSU] feel about [Greg] Sankey and their counterparts within the conference."

SEC ACCUSES LSU OF LETTING LANE KIFFIN RUN WILD AS EXPULSION VOTE COMING THURSDAY IN EXPLOSIVE COURT FILING

After the same judge granted Luis an injunction against the SEC that would prohibit them from punishing LSU if it were to roster and play the basketball star this season, a war of legal words has led to a massive kerfuffle within the legal circles.

The SEC stated that it would not impose any type of fines or penalties against LSU after the injunction was granted, but they were clearly testing Will Wade and the Tigers administration on whether they would actually put RJ Luis into a game.

ATTORNEY COMPARES SEC COMMISSIONER GREG SANKEY TO ‘KIM JONG’ IN LSU-RJ LUIS ELIGIBILITY LAWSUIT

On Tuesday, the SEC released a statement that clearly let it be known that they did not agree with how LSU was interpreting a court order. The Tigers did not have to make the decision on actually putting RJ Luis on the court, which is where the main course of this argument starts.

"LSU's decision today to rely on its own interpretation of the Court's order to justify its actions is inconsistent with the expectations and responsibilities of [SEC membership]. This is a deeply concerning and disappointing development."

On Wednesday night, the top officially blew off the lid. During their game against UL-Monroe, and mid-way through the first half, Will Wade subbed in RJ Luis.

"He was eligible, and he played," Will Wade said following LSU's win. 

The Tigers head coach did not discuss 

If there ever was an official escalation to a war, this was it.

Not only did LSU defy what the SEC President and Chancellors had voted on in the past three months, they were clearly jumping into the deep end of this very large pool of legal waters that will undoubtably set-off another chain of events that involve legal filings.

The conference wants to be able to enforce its own rules. LSU is using a court's order to waddle around the rules of rostering and playing a former professional athlete by using a Baton Rouge judge as the scapegoat.

INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN

In addition to the arguments made in a Louisiana court, the SEC had filed its own lawsuit against LSU on the same day Commissioner Greg Sankey took the stand in Baton Rouge.

In an Alabama federal court, the SEC sued LSU President Wade Rousse, athletic director Verge Ausberry and other Tiger officials for violating their first amendment rights pertaining to enforcing conference rules.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This has led to both sides exchanging legal jabs, with the latest coming on Wednesday, as the SEC was asking a judge to strike certain language used in a motion-to-dismiss filed by LSU. Legal counsel for the Tigers claimed that the SEC had brought forth "hallucinated" claims against defendants.

A judge ordered LSU lawyers to release a public apology through a press release, which Louisiana attorney general Liz Murrill told the court was not going to happen through her own filing.

In addition to the mess going on in an Alabama federal court, RJ Luis' attorney, Tony Clayton, filed a motion to hold the SEC in contempt of court that came in response to the conference's statement on Tuesday night.

"We want to hold [Sankey] and the SEC in contempt for the threat," Tony Clayton said. "Their lawyer sent us an email that they would not take any actions against LSU or threaten any actions. And then Sankey or an SEC official issued the threat about what they're going to do to LSU."

Now, ten minutes into a game against Louisiana-Monroe on Wednesday night, the LSU administration decided to pull the pin and throw the grenade.

item.title: 'The View' co-host Whoopi Goldberg demands Dems impeach RFK Jr, 'get his a-- out of there'
item.description: "The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg demanded Congress impeach HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. after the U.S. lost its measles elimination status Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
ABC's "The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg demanded that the incoming Democratic Congress impeach U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. after the country lost its measles elimination status Tuesday.

The panel on Wednesday's show discussed the Pan American Health Organization announcing that for the first time in 26 years, the U.S. lost its measles elimination status after more than 5,400 confirmed cases were reported this year.

The hosts largely blamed Kennedy for the outbreak, pointing to his past scrutiny of vaccines as a cause for the rise in cases, with Goldberg going as far as to hold him responsible for measles-related deaths.

RFK JR. BACKTRACKS ON TIMELINE FOR DETERMINING CAUSE OF AUTISM

"I’m just gonna say it: get his a-- out of there!" Goldberg said to a cheering audience. "Just impeach him! Impeach him! Impeach him. I don’t wanna say it, but I feel like he’s responsible for many people not making it. Get him gone, man!"

When co-host Joy Behar remarked that members of President Donald Trump's cabinet could still remain in office for two more years, Goldberg doubled down on Kennedy's impeachment.

"Start with this one!" Goldberg continued. "Start with this one, and then go to [Secretary of War Pete] Hegseth, and then go to the other ones, and get people in these positions who can actually do the damn job! We are tired of this! People are dying! Children are dying! Stop it! Impeach him!"

CHERYL HINES SAYS 'THE VIEW' HOSTS JUST WANTED TO 'GRILL' HER ABOUT RFK JR, DIDN'T TALK ABOUT NEW BOOK

In a comment to Fox News Digital, White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster defended Kennedy and said that the Trump administration has repeatedly encouraged measles vaccination, citing an ABC News interview with Trump from April 2025.

"President Trump and Secretary Kennedy have both stated that vaccination is the best way to prevent measles infections. In response to outbreaks, the President and Secretary have repeatedly encouraged measles vaccination, coordinated with states, and facilitated the deployment of vaccine doses across the country," Schuster said.

Fox News Digital also reached out to HHS and ABC for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

CNN'S DANA BASH SPARS WITH RFK JR OVER VACCINE EFFICACY, DEMANDS HE 'LOOK INTO THE CAMERA' AND PUSH VACCINES

"The View" panel has frequently criticized Kennedy's leadership, sometimes making extreme accusations. Earlier this year, Behar similarly accused Kennedy of "trying to kill us."

"Here you’ve got a guy who is in charge of our health, who is a former heroin addict ... he swam in sewage! Who does that?" Behar said in April. "And [he] snorted cocaine off a toilet seat. This is who is in charge of your health, America. We’re in a lot of trouble."

item.title: Fred Warner calls Mexico City NFL game 'super special' as Mexican roots take center stage
item.description: Fred Warner, who leads the 49ers with 88 tackles, calls returning to Mexico City "super special" as San Francisco preps at high elevation for the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
This week’s NFL international schedule will feature a return trip to Mexico City.

The San Francisco 49ers last played in Mexico City in 2022, and this Sunday they will be back in Mexico's capital city for a Week 11 matchup with the Minnesota Vikings. The trip also has personal significance for linebacker Fred Warner, whose maternal grandfather was born in Mexico.

Warner’s grandfather died when Warner’s mother, Laura, was young, and Warner never had the opportunity to meet him. He has nevertheless spoken about his connection to Mexican culture, including the Spanish language he heard and spoke at home as a child.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Warner acknowledged the significance of Sunday night's game.

"Super special," he said after practice on Wednesday. "I remember that first time around, didn’t know what exactly what to expect, but I think that was my first time being out of the country and playing in a game of that magnitude."

Warner, the NFL's current leading tackler, took in a World Cup match at Estadio Azteca over the summer and recalled the electric environment.

"That was elite," Warner said. "Soccer, or football as they call it, the World Cup, representing your home country, that is a whole different animal. The NFL obviously is elite as well, but that was that was a once-in-a-lifetime experience."

NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL CONFIRMS LEAGUE WANTS MULTIPLE TEAMS BASED OUTSIDE THE US: 'NO DOUBT'

San Francisco beat Arizona 38-10 in Mexico City on Nov. 21, 2022, and the team is following the same blueprint to prepare for Sunday night's game. After defeating the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday, the Niners flew to Colorado so they could practice at the Air Force Academy, where the 7,258-foot elevation is nearly equal to Mexico City, hoping to gain an advantage for the NFL’s final international game of 2026.

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan recalled some of the stressful elements that came along with the 2022 Mexico City trip, including the bus carrying players getting lost on the way to the stadium.

"Usually our last bus of players gets three hours before the game, and they got lost somehow on the way to the stadium," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "They didn’t get there until an hour and 15 minutes before the game, and had like 12 starters on it. So that was somewhat stressful, but it didn’t affect us."

The 49ers enter Sunday at 8-1 and atop the NFC standings. The Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins at last week's trade deadline, returning the veteran quarterback to the franchise where he spent six seasons.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: President Trump downplays panic over tech outages: ‘Nobody’s going to play games with us’
item.description: President Donald Trump urged Americans to "relax" over FAA and Microsoft outages, warning any country that targeted U.S. systems would be hit hard.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump sought to reassure Americans concerned about a series of technology disruptions over the past week, urging them to "relax" and saying no country would dare "play games" with U.S. digital infrastructure.

Trump’s remarks in China follow a slew of outages affecting the Federal Aviation Administration, Microsoft, major U.S. banks and other institutions, disrupting air travel and business operations and putting Americans on edge.

"Tell them to relax. Everything's good," the president told Fox News senior White House correspondent Jacqui Heinrich.

TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS

"I don't want to use specific names because they're treating me extremely well in China, and I have a lot of respect and a lot of relationships and a good relationship with President Xi. But if anybody did that to us, and we found out about it, they know what the repercussions would be with me," the commander in chief said on "The Ingraham Angle." 

"Nobody's going to play games with us."

Trump, who said the outages were unrelated, warned that any bad actors should know better than to target U.S. technological infrastructure.

"They know they would be hit so hard," the president said. 

RECENT SERVICE OUTAGES NOT STATE-SPONSORED ATTACKS, DNI JAY CLAYTON TESTIFIES

"These are individual events. ... I'll let you know if there's a problem."

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed Congress in part for the hours-long nationwide ground stop, arguing the system is outdated because the government has not provided the agency with sufficient funding to modernize its technology.

"They're putting in new equipment, and things happen when you put in new equipment," Trump said.

FORMER TOP FAA OFFICIAL WARNS OF 48-HOUR RECOVERY AFTER AGING TECH 'OVERWHELMED' AHEAD OF GROUND STOP

"This is 50-year-old equipment, and it has to be changed. And it's gone down before, and we did the right thing. Nobody was injured. Nobody was hurt. No planes were bunking into each other," he continued.

Trump told Fox News that Duffy is doing "fantastic," standing behind the transportation chief over his handling of Friday’s nationwide ground stop.

He echoed Duffy’s concerns about the state of the system, saying that while the United States has money available, he believes it is better to wait for additional funding and pursue a complete overhaul rather than "piecemeal," patchwork renovations.

"We were given $12 million, but I said, 'Don't spend it until we can do the whole thing, the whole system. You don't want to do piecemeal,'" Trump said.

"We want to give out ... like the big, beautiful deal, one big, beautiful contract," he proposed. "We want to give out a contract to somebody that can coordinate everything."

The president touted his building background and said that with his plan, the United States will have the best air traffic control system in the world.

"I build very well. I've made a lot of money building things, always, and I know how to do this stuff," he said.

item.title: Ella Langley dominates CMA Awards with major wins as Taylor Swift makes stunning return to stage
item.description: Ella Langley dominates the CMAs as she wins big while Taylor Swift makes her return after decade-long absence.
item.content:encoded:
The 60th annual Country Music Association Awards took place live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday night.

Ella Langley dominated the awards ceremony, as the winner of entertainer of the year, the biggest award of the night. 

While accepting the award, she joked that the crowd must be sick of her already, getting a laugh from those in the room.

"This isn't real life," she said while accepting the award. "Thank you Jesus, I'm at a loss for words," she added, before saying, "This has been the most special night.

As she swept all the categories she was nominated in, Lainey Wilson brought out a bedazzled broom for her, telling her she knew she had it prepared as she knew Langley was going to sweep the show. 

Langley also won music video of the year before the broadcast. "Choosin' Texas" was named as the music video of the year winner during Good Morning America Wednesday morning. The record-breaking hit, also won single of the year and song of the year. 

Later in the show, Langley got teary-eyed as she accepted the award for album of the year, for her album, "Dandelion," noting it took two years to make. She was speechless while accepting the award and received a standing ovation from the audience.

"I’m at a loss for words. I don’t know what to say," she said in her speech. "I love country music and I love what I do."

Her wins also resulted in two wins for Miranda Lambert, who is credited as a producer on the song. 

Langley continued her winning streak later on in the show when she took home the award for female vocalist of the year, beating out Lambert, Musgraves, Moroney and Wilson for the honor.

"I have so much love and respect for every single person and every single woman in this category," she said while accepting the award. "This is what I have lived and breathed not only just the past seven years that I moved to Nashville, but genuinely my whole entire life. I haven’t wanted to do another thing. There wasn’t anything on my heart. I never had a plan B. I was never gonna have a plan b. If I was still playing cover gigs with a tip jar out in front of me for four hours I’d still be doing this."

Rising star Langley led the pack with 9 nominations, tying Lainey Wilson and Lambert's all-time record for the most nods by a female artist in a single year. Her win for single of the year left Taylor Swift going home empty-handed tonight, which didn't stop Taylor Swift from cheering for her as she went up to accept the award.

Swift made her big return to the CMA Awards – after last attending in 2016. Her single, "I Knew It, I Knew You," is nominated for single of the year.

The singer took the stage to perform at the CMA Awards for the first time in 13 years, starting her performance with her nominated song, before transitioning into one of her classic hits, "Our Song." 

Lambert also had a moment on stage with Kacey Musgraves, when the two sang their hit duet, "Horses and Divorces," from Musgraves' latest album, "Middle of Nowhere."

The song references the rumored feud between the two singers, with them patching things up earlier this year.

Zach Top honored veteran and military families, bringing one on stage and surprising them with the return of their son from service.

In addition to her performance with Musgraves, Lambert took the stage once again with Langley to sing their song, "Snakeskin Boots" for the first time on television. The two matched in their versions of brown dresses with snakeskin print and fringe as they commanded the stage during their performance.

Parton was one of the most decorated figures in CMA Awards history, earning 45 nominations and winning 10 trophies over her career, including entertainer of the year in 1978, two female vocalist of the year awards, and the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016.

Beyond her wins, she also helped define the telecast itself, famously co-hosting the ceremony in 1988 and returning in 2019 to co-host alongside Carrie Underwood and Reba McEntire.

item.title: Alabama QB Keelon Russell's mother sues Marriott over twin's death, hotel counters with 911 audio
item.description: April Moore says a hotel worker knocked during CPR and no AED was available as she sues Marriott International over daughter Kierston Russell's death.
item.content:encoded:
April Moore, mother of Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell, is suing AC Hotel Tuscaloosa Downtown and Marriott International over the death of her daughter, Kierston Russell.

Details of the wrongful death suit surfaced ahead of a Dec. 7 hearing in Tuscaloosa County Circuit Court.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Russell has thrown for nearly 2,500 yards and 21 touchdowns this season. Off the field, his family is pursuing a jury trial over the events of June 3, 2025. Kierston, his 18-year-old twin sister, planned to enroll at Alabama alongside him.

Per defense filings, Moore and Keelon left their room around 7:20 p.m. after Kierston reported stomach pain and irregular sleep.

Moore returned, found Kierston unresponsive on the bathroom floor, called 911 at 9:55 p.m., and started CPR. Kierston died at DCH Regional Medical Center.

TWO MEN DIE AFTER SUSPECTED ELECTROCUTION AT HOTEL POOL AS RESCUE EFFORT INJURES OTHERS

Moore sued on June 15, 2026, accusing the hotel and Marriott of failing to train staff in CPR or provide a defibrillator. Her complaint states a worker knocked on the door during the emergency, forcing Moore to stop compressions to answer it, and offered no aid.

Plaintiff's attorney Derrick Mills said experts believe an AED would have saved Kierston's life, adding the hotel "literally frustrated April's efforts in trying to revive her daughter."

The defense disputes that account using timestamps.

In court filings, the defendants say 911 dispatchers never called the front desk, and staff responded only after a guest reported screaming. They contend 911 audio shows Moore never stopped CPR to open the door, requiring a worker to unlock it with a master key before EMTs began treatment within three minutes.

The defense also says 911 calls and bodycam photos place an AED in the room within three to five minutes, adding Alabama law did not require one. Defense counsel Rebecca Young declined comment.

To reach a jury under Alabama law, Moore must clear two hurdles: proving the hotel owed a duty beyond summoning paramedics, and proving its response cost Kierston her life.

Marriott and the hotel requested dismissal in October; Moore moved to seal records and filed a non-public response on Nov. 6, setting up a Dec. 7 showdown in court.

item.title: Bukele gets hero’s welcome from afar as thousands rally in Haiti after gang crackdown
item.description: Thousands marched in Haiti to thank Nayib Bukele for sending troops to battle violent gangs, prompting an emotional response from the Salvadoran president.
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of people in Haiti took to the streets Tuesday in a show of support for Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele deploying troops to the country to combat violent armed gangs.

The demonstration unfolded as Haiti's Minister of Justice and Public Security, Patrick Pélissier, prepared to travel to San Salvador to discuss anti-gang strategies and ongoing troop cooperation.

The president reflected on the moment in a post on X, sharing a video capturing a sea of people chanting, dancing and cheering in celebration.

"I never expected anything like this. I hear you loud and clear. I love you too. We will triumph. God will give us victory," Bukele said.

BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR

According to Reuters, some demonstrators carried signs reading "Long live Bukele" and "Down with the gangs," while others voiced their support for the Salvadoran leader.

"Only a week of operation, we can see the path to change in Haiti. We say thank you to Bukele for all the help he gives us," demonstrator Claudy Mayas said.

Another demonstrator said Bukele was providing Haitians with the one thing they had been waiting years for.

"Four years ago, I could not go to Champs de Mars. I couldn't go to the south of Haiti," a demonstrator, also identified as Claude, said.

"We don’t ask much of the government. We don’t ask for jobs. We need only security."

ROBOT DOGS MOUNTED WITH RIFLES DEPLOYED IN ANTI-GANG STADIUM OPERATION IN HAITI

Just two weeks ago, Bukele backed an operation involving devastating airstrikes that destroyed the headquarters of 400 Mawozo, one of Haiti's most powerful criminal gangs. The home of its leader, Lanmò San Jou, was also targeted in the operation, Bukele previously said.

The direct military action marked a dramatic escalation in Haiti's fight against years of severe gang violence and insecurity.

Bukele joined the mission after four Salvadoran members of the U.N.-backed anti-gang force went missing in a suspected gang ambush near Port-au-Prince on Oct. 18. At the time, Bukele sent more than 2,000 troops to Haiti.

EL SALVADOR-BACKED AIR ASSAULT DESTROYS HAITI GANG HEADQUARTERS AMID SEARCH FOR MISSING TROOPS

While residents paraded through the streets in celebration, U.N. officials issued a statement Tuesday reminding leaders that anti-gang operations must prioritize civilian protection.

"Security forces must strictly limit the use of lethal force to situations where it is unavoidable to protect life from an imminent threat and as a last resort," the agency said.

According to the U.N., armed gangs control an estimated 80% to 90% of Haiti's capital and are expanding into surrounding regions.

Between January and October 2026 alone, the U.N. documented nearly 4,600 people killed, alongside the wider displacement of nearly 1.5 million people.

item.title: Mayor of US city with largest Muslim population calls El-Sayed's election 'an American story'
item.description: Sen. Abdul El-Sayed's historic win drew praise from Dearborn's mayor, who calls the first Muslim American elected to the Senate a truly American story.
item.content:encoded:
The mayor of the first Arab-majority city in the U.S., home to one of the largest Muslim populations per capita in the nation, told Fox News Digital Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s election to the U.S. Senate was "monumental."

"It was monumental, and it's [truly] an American story where the brightest and best of us was elevated to one of the highest offices in the world — a member of the United States Senate — and where the people of Michigan elected an individual regardless of the direction in which he prays, but rather based on the direction in which he wishes to lead," Dearborn, Michigan, Mayor Abdullah Hammoud told Fox News Digital.

"I think that is truly a beautifully American story."

NYC'S MAMDANI SAYS ABDUL EL-SAYED'S SENATE VICTORY IN MICHIGAN 'MEANS SO MUCH TO SO MANY'

Hammoud's comments followed El-Sayed’s Nov. 3 victory over former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in Michigan's high-stakes race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. With the win, El-Sayed, a progressive Democrat and former Detroit health director, became the first Muslim American elected to the U.S. Senate.

In his victory speech in Detroit shortly after the race was called, El-Sayed took direct aim at the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC). The pro-Israel lobbying group and its affiliates poured roughly $30 million into the August Democratic primary to back U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens against El-Sayed, and he thanked the group for the chance to "beat you twice." 

Celebrating his victory, El-Sayed also invoked the Arabic phrase "Alhamdulillah," which translates to "Praise be to God."

ABDUL EL-SAYED DELIVERS MAJOR BLOW TO GOP IN MICHIGAN AFTER BRUISING SENATE RACE

Throughout the campaign, El-Sayed faced repeated scrutiny over his rhetoric on Israel, concerns among some Jewish voters in Michigan and allegations of family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, claims El-Sayed rejected. He also drew criticism from fellow Democrats over his campaign appearances alongside controversial far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who previously faced backlash over incendiary remarks regarding the Sept. 11 attacks and Israel.

Three days after his win, El-Sayed addressed the Arab America Foundation’s Connect Empowerment Summit in Chantilly, Virginia, just outside Washington, D.C., where he referred to Michigan as the "capital of Arab America."

"I know we’re here in D.C., which, of course, is the capital of the United States of America. But Michigan is the capital of Arab America," El-Sayed said.

During the speech, El-Sayed also pushed back against the attacks he faced on the campaign trail, saying opponents "wanted to make this a referendum on me and my name and my faith."

ASRA NOMANI: EL-SAYED GLIDES INTO ROLE AS ROCK STAR OF THE HARD LEFT'S RED-GREEN ALLIANCE

Hammoud, who became Dearborn’s first Arab American and Muslim mayor in 2022, explained to Fox News Digital what El-Sayed meant by calling Michigan the "capital of Arab America."

"I think he's just speaking to the idea that the largest concentration of Arab Americans happens to be in the city of Dearborn, just [as] you have so many other cities across America celebrating the unique demographic — sometimes the largest of X population residing within their city bounds — no different," Hammoud said.

item.title: Mamdani grilled on rhetoric toward Oct 7, combating antisemitism as Jewish New Yorkers fear current climate
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended his Oct. 7 X post at The New York Times' DealBook Summit, telling Andrew Ross Sorkin there must be room to mourn everyone.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani was grilled Wednesday on his efforts to combat antisemitism during his appearance at The New York Times DealBook Summit.

After greeting his "comrades" at the beginning of his sit-down, Mamdani was pressed by The New York Times' Andrew Ross Sorkin about the importance of "language," specifically in relation to the Jewish community in New York City and growing antisemitism.

Sorkin pointed to Mamdani's controversial X post commemorating the Oct. 7 terrorist attack committed against Israel, which dedicated more words toward the plight of the Palestinians and Israel's military response in Gaza than the roughly 1,200 Israelis who were brutally murdered that day by Hamas.

BILL MAHER MOCKS MAMDANI FOR PIVOTING TO ISRAEL CRITICISM IN OCT 7 TRIBUTE, CALLS IT 'TONE-DEAF'

"The head of the Reform Jewish movement (had) said at the time that they thought that the statement made New Yorkers less safe. And then there was a rabbi who said — they called himself a fan of yours — he said, 'Can we just have one day?'" Sorkin told Mamdani. 

"And I'm curious, again, about the language you use. And the reason I mention it is, you know, 53%, I think, of hate crimes in New York City are against Jews.

"And, so, when you use language in this regard — and I know we can have a whole debate about whether condemning Israel gets conflated with antisemitism and this and that — but do you feel like there's an extra sort of responsibility or distinction in the language you use when you use it?"

Mamdani pushed back at the premise of the question, saying his X post "doesn't cover the entirety of the day," which included a vigil honoring the Oct. 7 victims, noting that he was also protested for attending the vigil.

"My politics is one that believes that there has to be room to mourn everyone," Mamdani said. 

"And what I sought to do not only in the statement, but also in my physical attendance at that vigil, which I had attended the year before, was to make clear that I will oppose with every bone in my body the violations of international law, no matter who commits them, who conducts them. And that's why I've called Oct. 7 a war crime. And that is why I have also been immensely critical of the Israeli government as well."

MAMDANI DINED AT NYC RESTAURANT LINKED TO ANTI-ISRAEL MENU AFTER BEING BOOED AT OCT 7 VIGIL: REPORT

The democratic socialist mayor slammed the "objectionable" statistic that Jewish New Yorkers are the victims of more than half of all hate crimes despite being 10-12% of the city's population.

"That, to me, is unacceptable, because in addition to being proud of being the mayor of New York City, I'm also proud to be the mayor of the most Jewish city in the United States of America," Mamdani told Sorkin. 

"So much of what so many of us love about New York is tied up in that same legacy. And to me, the responsibility is you have to root out antisemitism. You have to root out any form of bigotry.

"And that there will be, and there are, Jewish New Yorkers, as well as New Yorkers of other faiths or no faiths at all, who disagree with me on my views on Israel and Palestine," the mayor continued. "There's no question. My job is to still deliver for them as well, and to deliver them the best possible city, because, at the end of the day, they live in the same city."

"I get it," Sorkin interjected. "My question is, would you ever think about sending out one tweet on Oct. 7, saying how terrible what happened on Oct. 7 was, and then waiting till Oct. 8 to say how terrible you think Israel has handled the situation?"

Sorkin's follow-up question sparked applause from the audience.

MAMDANI’S ANTISEMITISM PLAN DRAWS CRITICISM AS RABBIS SAY IT AVOIDS KEY DRIVER OF HATE

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

"When the Israeli government is conducting a genocide of Palestinians, oftentimes the defense that will be given, no matter what day that it's asked about, will be the relationship to Oct. 7," Mamdani responded. 

"My point being, this is a day that is not only a horrific war crime. It is also a day that has been used as a justification for all that followed it. And it is in that day that it is important, like in any day, to mourn the totality of its impact."

Mamdani insisted he understands "the other side" of the argument but doubled down on his stance.

"I have a politics of universality. Whenever I'm asked about 'Why do you support Palestinian freedom or Palestinian rights?' I speak about the importance of extending these same values, of empathy. And that is who I am," he added.

"I'm gonna keep that to myself."

Those six words were the lone answer Dallas Cowboys star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams offered to reporters on Wednesday. Reporters kept peppering the four-time Pro Bowler with questions, and he just repeated those same six words 12 times over.

After the Cowboys' defense was gashed for 584 total yards by the San Francisco 49ers in their 46-20 loss on Sunday, the team stripped play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Mike Pettine will now call the defensive plays for the Cowboys.

The rest of the NFC East has been ravaged with injuries and underperformance, yet the Cowboys, despite remaining largely healthy, have been unable to take advantage. The New York Giants lead the division at 5-3-1 despite having started three different quarterbacks after Jaxson Dart's injury.

item.title: Obama-era homeless policy fueled crisis it promised to end, expert says as Trump admin makes striking reversal
item.description: Homeless services veteran Michele Steeb says LA’s funding cutoff offers a chance to restore accountability after years of alleged mismanagement.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration’s decision to permanently cut federal funding to Los Angeles’ scandal-plagued homeless agency marks a stunning reversal of an Obama-era policy that one expert said produced massive failures.

In an interview with Fox News Digital, homeless services veteran Michele Steeb broke down Tuesday’s announcement from the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that it is severing ties with the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA).

Steeb said the Housing First model adopted by LAHSA, which provides housing unconditionally without requiring individuals to pursue sobriety or mental health treatment, was championed by former President Barack Obama. 

HUD’S HOMELESSNESS REFORMS PUT HUMAN LIVES AHEAD OF HOUSING BUREAUCRACY

She argued the model discouraged recovery by allowing people to remain in subsidized housing indefinitely, leaving fewer available units for others seeking permanent housing.

"So, back in 2013, when they instituted this, President Obama promised that this very different approach would end homelessness in a decade. And a decade later, we were at an almost 35% increase with no accountability," Steeb said, referring to the national homeless population.

The program ultimately "eliminates purpose from individuals," Steeb said. "They're given housing for life without any requirements."

Earlier this year, Obama called Los Angeles' homelessness crisis a moral "atrocity," arguing that homelessness programs must pair assistance with accountability.

"We should recognize that the average person doesn’t want to have to navigate around a tent city in the middle of downtown," Obama said. "That’s a losing political strategy."

EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE LA'S HOMELESS HELLSCAPE — UNLIKELY CRITICS BLAST DEMS AS GOP HOPEFUL TOURS SKID ROW

California, which adopted the model statewide, offers a particularly striking example of what Steeb views as its shortcomings. Despite significant government investment, homelessness has continued to climb rather than move toward the promised goal of ending it.

Steeb said homelessness in California surged 40% between 2016 and 2025, even as federal spending on homelessness increased at least 200% under the Housing First approach instituted in 2013.

The situation has been particularly stark in Los Angeles, where homelessness climbed between 60% and 70% over the past five years despite LAHSA receiving more than $1 billion in federal funding.

LA HOMELESSNESS FRAUD CASES EXPOSE DEEPER PROBLEM THAN STOLEN MILLIONS, OVERSIGHT HAWK WARNS

Steeb said, despite the mounting evidence of failure, defenders of the system continued to blame the homelessness crisis on insufficient funding.

"It's a shame to me that the system, what I often call the homeless industrial complex, is trying to defend it," she said.

"It just has failed so massively. So, there's no excuses except that it was the wrong approach."

Steeb said HUD's settlement represents an effort by the Trump administration to restore accountability to homeless services after LAHSA became embroiled in allegations of fraud and financial mismanagement.

The agency's funding will soon be transferred to Los Angeles County, according to officials.

Although Steeb acknowledged the county has its own problems, she hopes the transition could improve a system she believes has failed to address the crisis.

"I'm hopeful. … I think it's better than LAHSA, but I don't think it's going to be that much better," Steeb said.

item.title: No 1 Florida loses to Houston as four of the preseason AP top five fall before Thanksgiving
item.description: Dedan Thomas Jr. scored 30 as No. 8 Houston avenged its 2025 national title loss by beating No. 1 Florida 86-76, handing the Gators their first loss.
item.content:encoded:
Houston had waited since April 2025 for another shot at Florida. On Wednesday, the Cougars made sure this one would not be decided in the final minute.

No. 8 Houston beat No. 1 Florida 86-76 in Las Vegas, advancing to the Players Era 8 championship game and handing the Gators their first loss of the season. Florida had beaten Houston 65-63 in the 2025 national championship game. Florida’s loss also means four of the preseason AP top five have already been beaten, with Duke losing twice.

Florida, which was the AP preseason No. 1 and entered the game 5-0, led 40-37 at halftime. Houston took the lead early in the second half before Florida briefly regained the lead at 47-46. But Houston scored the next 11 points and never trailed again, building a lead as large as 14 points.

Dedan Thomas Jr. scored 30 for the Cougars, while Joseph Tugler recorded a 12-point, 10-rebound double-double.

KENTUCKY NEEDS BUZZER-BEATING THREE TO SURVIVE NORTHERN ARIZONA'S UPSET BID AT RUPP ARENA

Kelvin Sampson’s Houston program entered the game ranked eighth and has been among the sport’s contenders for years. Still, beating the team that denied Houston a national title, and doing it while that team sat at No. 1, gives the Cougars a massive November resume boost.

It also makes the analytics look pretty smart. The AP voters had Houston 10th in the preseason, but KenPom rated the Cougars third. After beating Florida by 10 on a neutral floor, Houston looks a lot closer to No. 3 than No. 10.

Florida joins Duke, Illinois and Arizona as preseason AP top five teams that have already lost less than three weeks into the college basketball season. UConn is the lone unbeaten member of that group, at least heading into its Wednesday night visit to Arizona.

Arizona was the first to fall, losing 84-75 to UCLA on opening night. The Wildcats are ranked No. 12 in this week's poll. A week later, Michigan State beat then-No. 2 Duke 79-73, while Texas Tech knocked off then-No. 3 Illinois 84-78.

Illinois responded Tuesday by going into Duke and winning by 21. The Blue Devils, the preseason No. 2, have now lost twice before Thanksgiving. The Michigan State loss only dropped Duke from No. 2 to No. 5, but expect another fall for the Blue Devils when the Week 4 rankings come out on Nov. 23.

Michigan State’s stay at No. 2 may be short, too. After beating Duke, the Spartans managed just 46 points in a 61-46 loss at No. 14 Tennessee on Tuesday.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And the trouble has reached beyond the preseason favorites. Unranked Memphis opened its season by beating No. 18 Iowa State 80-76. The Tigers followed that by erasing an 18-point deficit against No. 10 Louisville on Sunday and winning 98-78 after outscoring Louisville by 31 points in the second half.

Over the weekend, LSU went to Gonzaga and beat the then-No. 14 Bulldogs 81-80 on a late shot. On Tuesday, Indiana added an 81-76 win over No. 20 Arkansas.

Kentucky can be grateful it is missing from that list. The Wildcats, who entered the game as 30-point favorites, needed a late three-pointer to escape Northern Arizona 78-77 at Rupp Arena last week, a close call that fit the season’s mood even if it didn't count as another upset.

None of this settles who will matter in March because there is still a lot of basketball to play. I'm certainly not ready to write off Florida, Duke, Arizona or Illinois because of an early-season hiccup (or two, in Duke's case).

Still, that’s five losses for the preseason AP top five. The voters put Florida first and Michigan State second on Monday. By Wednesday night, both had lost by double digits. Good luck with next Monday’s ballot (If the AP has a spare one, I’ll take it).

item.title: Iran warns Bahrain monarchy its survival is at risk amid push to 'evict' US Fifth Fleet
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned Bahrain's monarchy its survival is in doubt as drones and missiles hit the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet home.
item.content:encoded:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned Wednesday that Bahrain's monarchy faces an existential threat as Iranian drones and missiles targeted U.S. military installations in the Gulf kingdom.

Tehran's warning came amid renewed attacks on Bahrain, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, and a regional expert warned of Iran's decades-long efforts to destabilize the island nation and assert territorial claims.

"This is a regime that has tried to inflame tensions there for quite literally several decades and has claims to the island nation as well," Behnam Ben Taleblu, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), told Fox News Digital.

BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES

"The Islamic Republic is also trying to use military force to evict the United States from the region," he added.

In a warning directed at Bahrain's ruling Al Khalifa family, IRGC Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi accused the monarchy of cooperating with military action against Iran, relying on U.S. protection and challenging Shiite religious authority.

"Colluding in the aggression against Islamic Iran, living inside the American security bubble, and encroaching on the authority of the Shiite religious leadership are three fundamental mistakes being made by the Al Khalifa regime," Mohebbi wrote on X.

IRAN VOWS ‘ASTONISHING’ STRIKES AND LIFTS MISSILE-RANGE LIMIT AS US TARGETS LAND ROUTES

"If it persists in them, its survival under the new regional security order will be in doubt," he warned.

"A word to the wise is enough."

Mohebbi's threat also followed a Bahraini crackdown on Shiite religious leaders.

On Monday, a criminal court sentenced dozens of Shiite clerics to life in prison on terrorism-related charges after prosecutors accused them of collaborating with Iran and plotting to undermine the government.

Bahrain's Public Prosecution agency said investigators uncovered communications between some defendants and Iranian authorities, including the IRGC, and accused the clerics of supporting terrorism and sabotage aimed at overthrowing the monarchy.

"The Islamic Republic has a panoply of gripes against Bahrain as well as against the ruling royal family of that country," Taleblu said.

"Some are sectarian, some are political, some are strategic, and some, again, have to do with the U.S. force presence in the region," the expert explained.

IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS

Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, a critical hub for American naval operations across the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters.

The latest regional escalation follows repeated Iranian drone attacks targeting American military equipment in Bahrain, including a U.S. radar installation Tehran claimed to have targeted for the third time in less than a week. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said the attacks were intercepted.

Bahrain also reported intercepting Iranian attacks early Wednesday, a day after the IRGC claimed to have struck a base used by American forces.

"The regime is also looking for places close to its territory where it can land blows against the U.S.—as well as against the order that has allowed the U.S. to be in the region for quite some time—and to be able to do so on the cheap," Taleblu said.

IRAN ESCALATES IN HORMUZ, CLAIMS STRIKE ON OMANI ISLAND IT SAYS 'ENEMY' USES FOR US MILITARY OPS

"They want to be able to generate pain against the U.S. more broadly in the region and do so in places that have already been hit."

Taleblu also said Iran's strategy is designed not only to damage American military assets but to increase pressure on Bahrain's monarchy to reconsider hosting U.S. forces.

"They've done this to limit the space for the U.S. to actually operate from the region and try to create tougher political conditions for the ruling family in that country to keep that U.S. force presence there."

He warned that the growing missile and drone threat could force Washington to reassess its long-term military presence in the Persian Gulf.

"Now that the war is out of the shadows and the weapons being used are missiles and drones, the future of the U.S. footprint in the region will be based on whether America can afford to build and defend bases so close to an adversary's territory under fire," Taleblu said.

"The test case as to what the U.S. does with the Fifth Fleet in Bahrain, and with the radars in that country, could actually be a harbinger of what the future of the U.S. footprint in the CENTCOM AOR — and in particular, the Persian Gulf region — looks like post-war with Iran," he added.

item.title: Tyler Herro's three-words sums up status with ex-teammate Bam Adebayo for first game since punching incident
item.description: Tyler Herro says he hasn't talked to Bam Adebayo as the Miami Heat host the Bucks in their first meeting since the reported Summer League altercation.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Heat welcomed the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night in a matchup that might otherwise blend into the early-season NBA schedule.

But a summer feud involving a former Heat player and one of Miami’s current stars has added an unexpected layer of intrigue to the matchup. In July, tensions between Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro reportedly boiled over in Las Vegas.

Since the dispute between the two NBA stars, questions have lingered over whether Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro had repaired their relationship or whether tensions remained.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Wednesday marked the first time the two players faced each other since the incident, and Herro was noncommittal when asked about the state of their relationship.

HEAT VS. BUCKS BEST BETS: GIANNIS GETS HIS FIRST SHOT AT MILWAUKEE

"I'm not sure. I haven't talked to him," Herro told reporters Wednesday.

Adebayo and Herro were involved in a physical altercation at an NBA Summer League practice facility, during which the Heat center allegedly struck the Milwaukee Bucks guard in the head area.

A blockbuster deal over this past offseason sent Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami and Herro to Milwaukee, ending his time as Adebayo’s Heat teammate.

MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS

Herro reflected on his time sharing a locker room with Adebayo, and praised the three-time All-Star's skillset. "Obviously I spent a lot of time with Bam. I admire his game. He's a great player. Can do everything on the floor, guard 1-5. He's gifted offensively."

Sources told ESPN that Adebayo initially confronted Herro over alleged social media comments criticizing his defense. Screenshots circulated online purportedly showed Herro questioning Adebayo’s defensive prowess in an Instagram direct message with a fan.

Adebayo agreed to a three-year, $166 million extension with Miami in June 2024. The alleged DM also appeared to question whether his nightly defensive effort justified a salary approaching $60 million.

Miami entered Wednesday night with an 8-6 record, while Milwaukee had won just once this season.

item.title: Patrick McEnroe joins Rep Tim Walberg to back Team USA Act capping foreign college athletes at 20% of rosters
item.description: Outside the U.S. Capitol, Patrick McEnroe backed the TEAM USA Act, citing nearly 70% foreign Division I tennis rosters as U.S. taxpayers fund Olympians.
item.content:encoded:
Outside the U.S. Capitol on Wednesday, International Tennis Hall of Fame President Patrick McEnroe backed the TEAM USA Act, calling for a 20% cap on international recruits to safeguard college spots for American kids.

Speaking with OutKick after a joint press conference with House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg, McEnroe warned that foreign recruits hold nearly 70 percent of Division I tennis spots while U.S. taxpayers train hundreds of rival Olympians.

According to House Education and Workforce Committee data, the number of international athletes receiving college scholarships has nearly tripled since 2001, surging from roughly 8,945 to about 25,000 today.

PATRICK MCENROE ON U.S. OPEN WEED SMELL, TRANS ATHLETES, FOREIGN RECRUITS RESHAPING COLLEGE TENNIS

Without roster limits, college programs have turned into feeders for overseas pros, and only a strict cap can save spots for young Americans.

"Well, I think there is a good chance that we can push this through, which would limit the amount of international athletes in our collegiate system to 20%, which I think is quite fair," McEnroe told OutKick.

During Wednesday's press conference, Chairman Walberg pressed the urgency of his bill, formally titled the Training and Education for American Members in University Sports and Athletics Act (H.R. 10351).

McEnroe, who played college tennis at Stanford University in the 1980s, welcomes international competition, but noted that foreign enrollment on varsity rosters has climbed over the past 15 years, crowding American-born players out of U.S. universities.

"The numbers are stratospheric," McEnroe stated.

"I mean, it is closing in on 70% for Division I tennis players. Both male and female are in the mid-60s at the moment, and it is continuing to rise. And you are seeing it in other sports as well. Men's soccer is well over 50% now, and many rosters are pretty much 100% international athletes.

I’M A COLLEGE ATHLETE. THE SYSTEM THAT GAVE ME MY DREAM IS STARTING TO BREAK

"I do not think that is good for the ecosystem of youth sports."

Coaches have privately told McEnroe they welcome a cap to break the cycle, though few will risk their jobs by speaking out. Across college athletics, whether a football coach earns $15 million or a tennis coach makes $150, 000, athletic departments demand immediate wins, and job survival pushes programs toward older overseas talent.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"When you see your big rival down the block getting the best players they can from Europe, well, you are going to say you have got to stay in the game, so you are going to do the same thing," McEnroe explained.

"So in no way do I blame the coaches nor the athletes who are just looking for the opportunity, whether they come from Serbia, England, or Tennessee. But the kids in our country are losing opportunities. That is just the bottom line."

That recruiting arms race is hollowing out American youth sports.

A homegrown player who easily earned a spot on a top 50 tennis roster a decade ago is now shut out, leaving parents of 12- to 14-year-old prospects questioning the steep costs and years of sacrifice required for elite junior training when scholarships go to imported semi-professionals.

Rebuilding that domestic pipeline, McEnroe argued, starts with giving coaches clear guardrails.

"I think they would like to have a choice where they can get two players on their team that are international, and the rest we can make up with American kids," he noted.

SENATE MOVES TO REIN IN COLLEGE SPORTS 'WILD WEST' WITH SWEEPING NEW RULES FOR PLAYERS, SCHOOLS

"Last time I checked, the college system in sports was not supposed to be professional. I realize we sort of lost the plot there when it comes to football and basketball, but all the Olympic sports should just be training grounds for young kids and places where you can dream, have a goal, accomplish that goal, and get an education."

At Wednesday's press conference, Walberg spotlighted that paradox using the Paris Olympic Games.

While 65% of Team USA athletes had ties to NCAA athletics, only 385 of the 1,036 NCAA Olympians in Paris represented the United States, with the remaining 63% competing for foreign nations.

In effect, U.S. universities backed by state and federal tax dollars are funding the training of athletes who later compete against America on the Olympic stage. McEnroe and Walberg argue foreign governments should fund their own Olympic programs rather than relying on American taxpayers.

Under the TEAM USA Act, a uniform 20 percent cap would apply across every collegiate sport, limiting a 10-player college tennis roster to two international spots. Holding every school and coach to one rule would halt the arms race while preserving most roster spots for American athletes.

Passing the bill requires bipartisan support in the House and Senate, where Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) introduced companion legislation. Alongside Walberg, McEnroe briefed lawmakers on the roster data, warning that many in Washington remain unaware of how dramatically college sports have shifted.

Without congressional action, McEnroe cautions, opportunities for American families will keep shrinking.

At stake is the future of the 99 percent of college athletes who never turn pro, and whether higher education preserves varsity sports as an avenue for education, character, and upward mobility.

"This is the American collegiate system, right? It is not international. It is not a professional sport," McEnroe told OutKick.

"College sports was started, and has given so many people the opportunity, because of what it is supposed to do, which is help people get an education, better their lives, and be useful members of society. That is why I am here, and that is what I am trying to help and protect."
