item.title: Wife and daughter arrested after DNA IDs man whose severed head was found in trash bag
item.description: Mary Fitzmaurice allegedly kept collecting her father's Social Security and pension benefits after his death, telling relatives he was still alive.
item.content:encoded:
A California woman and her daughter were arrested more than four years after a woman walking her dog found a man's severed head in a trash bag, authorities said.

The Placer County Sheriff’s Office identified the man as Paul Wesley Fitzmaurice Jr., 73, who had never been reported missing. Authorities said his wife and daughter had told relatives the victim was still alive.

His daughter, 45-year-old Mary Fitzmaurice, and his wife, 75-year-old Georgia "Gwenn" Fitzmaurice, were booked into the South Placer Jail on Tuesday, officials said in a news release. 

Mary was booked on suspicion of murder and Gwenn on suspicion of being an accessory.

DNA BREAKTHROUGH LEADS TO ARREST IN GRISLY 33-YEAR-OLD COLD CASE INVESTIGATORS NEVER GAVE UP ON

The women "kept up the facade to family and friends that Paul was still alive," Placer County Sheriff Wayne Woo said at a news conference Wednesday. He said they continued receiving Fitzmaurice’s Social Security benefits and California public pension after his death.

Woo said the women told some of Fitzmaurice’s estranged relatives "he was being a recluse, and he would disappear for days at a time." 

They claimed he "would come back to the house every week or so and stay for a couple of days," Woo said.

In its news release, the sheriff’s office alleged Mary killed her father and the two women "conspired to dispose of his remains."

At Wednesday’s news conference, Placer County District Attorney Morgan Gire said prosecutors expected to file a murder charge against Mary Fitzmaurice by the end of the day and were weighing additional charges related to the killing and the collection of Fitzmaurice’s benefits.

Asked whether money was a motive, Woo said, "There’s still a lot of investigative work to be done, and I would be speculating on motive at this point."

NEW CALIFORNIA LAW EXPANDS DNA TOOLS FOR MISSING PERSONS INVESTIGATIONS

The dog walker found the bag on Sept. 28, 2022, in the Todd Valley area of Foresthill while the Mosquito Fire was burning nearby. Woo said the discovery drew little attention at the time.

"The people that didn’t forget about this case is the residents of Foresthill and our cold case detectives," Woo said.

The remains were too decomposed for investigators to identify the man. Forensic experts at California State University, Chico, helped produce an artist’s rendering, but it yielded no match in missing-person cases. A search of the national law enforcement DNA database also came up empty.

In January 2024, detectives sent a DNA sample to Othram Labs, which used forensic genetic genealogy to find possible distant relatives. With the FBI’s help, investigators traced the family tree and obtained a DNA sample from an out-of-state relative that helped confirm Fitzmaurice’s identity.

GIRL KNOWN AS 'CHELSEA JANE DOE' ID'D 26 YEARS AFTER MUTILATED BODY FOUND HUNDREDS OF MILES FROM HOME STATE

Othram said in a news release that Fitzmaurice’s identification marked the 94th publicly announced case in California in which investigators used its technology to identify someone.

The sheriff’s office said in its release that investigators believe Mary killed her father at the family’s Citrus Heights home, which detectives searched Tuesday with help from the FBI. 

When asked at the briefing where Fitzmaurice was killed, Woo said, "With evidence that we gathered and collected yesterday, we’ll hopefully determine that."

Woo said the rest of Fitzmaurice’s remains have yet to be found. 

"We did not find any remains at the residence yesterday," he said.

item.title: Muslims poised to outnumber Christians globally by 2035 amid demographic shifts
item.description: Pew Research Center study projects Muslims will outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, driven by higher fertility rates and younger populations.
item.content:encoded:
People practicing the Islamic faith are poised to outnumber Christians globally by 2035, becoming the world's largest religion, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Center.

The detailed report attributes the shift primarily to higher fertility rates and younger populations among Muslims, who are growing at a faster rate than other major faiths.

"Around the world, we find that Muslims tend to have more children than non-Muslims, [and] they tend to be younger as a result of having more children in the past," Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett told Fox News Digital.

WHY PEOPLE REALLY STOPPED HAVING KIDS: NEW STUDY UNCOVERS THE SURPRISING REASONS FAMILIES ARE SHRINKING

Muslims have the highest fertility rate at 3.1 children per woman, followed by Christians at 2.5, according to the study. Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women gave birth to 252 million babies, more than women of any other religion and compared to 208 million born to Christian mothers.

If trends continue, the United States will also undergo a major religious shift. While Christians currently account for roughly 62% to 64% of U. S. adults, that share is expected to fall below 50% by 2065.

POLL FINDS SHARP RISE IN YOUNG MEN CALLING RELIGION 'VERY IMPORTANT'

By 2070, Christians are projected to make up less than half of the U. S. population, while religiously unaffiliated individuals, known as "nones," will rise to about 41%.

"The Muslim population in the U. S. is growing faster than the Christian population, but Christians vastly outnumber Muslims in the U. S., and that's not going to change," Hackett said.

By 2070, the Muslim population in the U. S. is expected to increase to nearly 4%, making Muslims the third-largest group in the country behind Christians and the religiously unaffiliated, surpassing the U.S. Jewish population.

Globally, the demographic center of major faiths is also moving. By 2070, Pakistan is projected to have the largest Muslim population, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia, which currently has the largest Muslim population of any country.

POPE LEO XIV TO VISIT FASTEST-GROWING CATHOLIC CONTINENT DURING 4-NATION AFRICA TRIP

Meanwhile, the presence of Christianity is shifting southward. By 2070, more than half of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo is projected to surpass the U.S. as the country with the single greatest number of Christians.

A century ago, most of the world's Christians lived in Europe, Hackett noted. However, Europe's population is now growing slowly and expected to shrink in the coming decades, while Africa's population expands rapidly.

"Europe's population has been growing slowly, and Africa's population has been growing very quickly," Hackett said. "In the coming decades, Europe's population is expected to shrink, [while] Africa's population is going to expand a lot."

Other religious demographics are shifting as well. The global Jewish population is expected to become increasingly concentrated, with 62% living in Israel by 2070, up from 46% in 2020.

AGE OF FIRST-TIME MOTHERS HITS RECORD HIGH IN BLUE STATES AS BIRTH RATES KEEP FALLING

In addition, the global Muslim population is projected to exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, compared to just under 3 billion Christians, according to Pew.

Overall, Muslims and Christians are the only major religious groups projected to keep pace with the world's overall population growth, which is expected to increase by 29% between 2020 and 2070. Christians are projected to grow by 30% and Muslims by 80%.

GEN Z FLOCKING TO CATHOLIC CHURCHES IN NYC FOR YOUTH GROUPS, SOCIAL EVENTS AMID CONVERSION BOOM

Beyond organized religions, many countries continue to see a surge in "nones," those with no religious affiliation, atheists or agnostics.

While China holds a massive proportion of the world's religiously unaffiliated, its population decline will offset growth elsewhere, Hackett said. Excluding China, the global population of "nones" is projected to grow by more than 180 million by 2070.

The religiously unaffiliated already account for a majority of the population in 10 countries, including the Czech Republic, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Uruguay and Vietnam.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Bucket list vacation destination just got a lot tougher for Americans to reach
item.description: U.S. airlines are cutting seats to popular vacation destination Costa Rica this winter, with January capacity down 12.5%, and San José hit harder than Liberia as airfares climb.
item.content:encoded:
American travelers heading to a popular vacation getaway could face fewer flight options and higher airfares during the busy winter vacation season.

Airlines are scheduling fewer flights and offering fewer seats from the U.S. to Costa Rica in December and January compared with last year, according to flight schedule data from Cirium, an aviation analytics company that tracks airline operations worldwide. 

The drop is expected to be especially noticeable after the holidays. In January, the number of available seats from the U.S. to Costa Rica is scheduled to fall 12.5% compared to a year earlier.

BUDGET AIRLINE EXPANDS ITS FOOTPRINT WITH 11 NEW TROPICAL FLIGHT ROUTES BEGINNING IN NOVEMBER

San José appears to be taking a bigger hit than Liberia, which serves the popular beaches and resorts of Costa Rica's Guanacaste region.

Advance bookings to San José for December and January are lagging behind last year, according to Cirium. Liberia is also seeing a decline.

Cirium cautioned that the booking figures do not include all reservations made directly with airlines.

The changes follow several airline service reductions this year. 

JetBlue suspended service from Orlando, while Frontier paused its San José flights between August and October, according to an October report from Costa Rica's Center for Tourism Studies (CET).

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The decline has been more pronounced in San José. 

In October, the airport there had 70 fewer weekly flights than a year earlier, while Liberia gained 10, the report found.

For Americans eyeing a Costa Rica getaway, the decline in service comes as ticket prices are also climbing.

Cirium data shows airfares from the U.S. were higher throughout the first eight months of 2026 than during the same period in 2025.

By August, the average fare had reached about $391, compared with roughly $276 a year earlier.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The reduction in flights is particularly significant for Costa Rica, where the U.S. accounts for nearly half of the country's scheduled airline seats, according to CET. 

Tourism is also a major source of revenue for the country, generating about $5.54 billion in 2025, according to data from the Costa Rican Tourism Institute.

While fewer seats do not necessarily mean fewer tourists will ultimately visit, the changes could leave some American travelers with fewer nonstop flights to choose from as they plan winter trips.

Guanacaste has also drawn attention from U.S. travelers for a separate health concern this year.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued a Level 2 Travel Health Notice for the province in July amid a chikungunya outbreak, Fox News Digital previously reported, with most reported cases centered around the popular beach destination of Playa Langosta.

The CDC advised travelers visiting the area to take extra precautions against mosquito bites, including using insect repellent and wearing long-sleeved shirts and pants.

item.title: Carville dares far-left to 'run somebody' against mainstream Dems in primary and end their 'civil war'
item.description: James Carville challenged the far-left wing of the Democratic Party to test its popularity and run a dream candidate against mainstream rivals in the 2028 presidential primary.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville challenged far-left Democrats to pick a candidate to represent them and see how well that candidate performs against mainstream Democrats in the 2028 presidential primary.

Carville argued on his "Politics War Room" podcast that, after briefly uniting to win a coalition victory against President Donald Trump, the Democratic Party is now due for a "civil war" among its ranks. However, he suggested the far left had overestimated its popularity. 

Carville challenged the progressives in his party to run their ideal candidate in the Democratic primary and let voters decide.

"The opinion that should matter, the most important opinion in all of this are people that vote in Democratic primaries for president of the United States," he said.

JAMES CARVILLE PREDICTS A 2028 'RECKONING' AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATES EYE THE DEMOCRATIC TICKET

"Stop running your mouth and run somebody," Carville said. "This is my proposal. You rally around a candidate that embodies the message and the values of ‘true progressivism.’ This is ‘Medicare-for-all.’ This is ‘question the very fundamental value of capitalism.’ 'We're not for incremental change. We're for change.’ Run somebody."

Carville said the candidate would be welcome at any debate and, if anything, would likely be favored by the media over mainstream candidates.

"I got news for you. The f---ing press will be pulling for you. OK?" he said.

"So, you're going to have a lot of advantages going in," Carville continued. "You're going to have a very sympathetic press. You're going to have a singular person that you and all of your friends and people that think like you, can all rally around.

"And then let's accept the verdict of the voters that vote in Democratic primaries for president of the United States."

JAMES CARVILLE WARNS FAR-LEFT CANDIDATES 'TOO HARD-HEADED' TO KNOW THEY'RE UNPOPULAR

Carville argued that the primary would test whether "your message is so popular that there are tens of millions or hundreds of millions of people that are dormant and waiting to be activated at the sound of the true bugle of progressivism, and they'll rise up in untold numbers."

However, he warned that every candidate should be asked on stage if they would support the eventual Democratic presidential nominee. If progressive candidates refuse to do so, he challenged them to reveal this upfront.

"But g--damn it, let's trust the Democratic primary voter," he suggested. "Yeah, that's a unique idea that maybe voters have a say so in this."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Democratic strategist Julian Epstein told Fox News Digital he disagreed with Carville's argument.

"There is a complete contradiction in this soliloquy," he said. "On the one hand, he is saying the elites should pick a progressive candidate. In the next breath, he says the voters should choose. The bigger issue is that this eludes the more fundamental challenge facing the Democrats.

"Democrats still have a toxic brand with about 28% of voters approving it and about 7-in-10 voters thinking the party's out of touch," Epstein said. "The party is far to the left of the median voter. The presidential primary process, with the activists and the NGO industrial complex, will pull the party further to the left.

"The answer is finding a modern-day equivalent of a Bill Clinton who has the personal charisma and the policy ingenuity to say no to the radical left and to meet the voters where they are," he continued. "We have been, and continue to be, a center-right country.

"The socialist movement may be in touch with the rage culture of influencer social media, but they are out of touch with the average voter," Epstein added. 

"This is the paradox the Democratic Party has to figure out. Progressive elites selecting a candidate before the primary is totally besides the point."
